title: Twelve thousand cells, six patients
study: 3 patients per subtype; 12,000 cells total.
analysis: Pool cells and run cell-level Wilcoxon DEG.
question: What is the main inference problem?
betterApproach: Use patient×cell-type pseudobulk or a justified hierarchical model; report per-patient effects and FDR.
maximalConclusion: In sampled cells, expression differs descriptively; patient-level subtype inference is not established.

title: Survival HR without time zero
study: Retrospective treatment cohort with treatment started at varying times.
analysis: Classify ever-treated patients as treated from diagnosis and fit Cox regression.
question: Which design error comes before interpreting the HR?
expectedFindings: Exposure is defined using future information
Adjusted Cox covariates do not repair time misclassification
betterApproach: Use a time-varying exposure, landmark design with explicit target population, or target-trial emulation.
maximalConclusion: No treatment effect conclusion is supportable from the reported analysis.

title: Significant here, not there
study: Randomized trial reports treatment effects by sex.
analysis: Men: HR .72, P=.03; women: HR .91, P=.31.
question: What statistical comparison is missing?
betterApproach: Test a prespecified treatment×sex interaction on a defined scale and interpret uncertainty.
maximalConclusion: Evidence supports an overall effect and uncertain subgroup estimates, not proven sex-specific efficacy.

title: AUC from the training set
study: A 60-gene recurrence model is developed in 90 patients.
analysis: Features and coefficients chosen on all data; training AUC=.94.
claim: The model has excellent predictive accuracy.
question: What evidence is missing?
betterApproach: Repeat the full pipeline in bootstrap/nested CV, then evaluate a locked model externally.
maximalConclusion: The model fits the development data; out-of-sample performance is unknown.

title: Calibration by Hosmer–Lemeshow
study: A diagnostic model is tested in 1,500 patients.
analysis: Report C=.81 and Hosmer–Lemeshow P=.18.
question: Why is this insufficient?
expectedFindings: Non-significance is not evidence of good calibration
betterApproach: Report calibration-in-the-large, slope, flexible calibration plot, and uncertainty.
maximalConclusion: The model discriminates moderately; calibration has not been adequately characterized.

title: Complete cases only
study: Prognostic cohort has 28% missing performance status, concentrated among sick patients.
analysis: Delete incomplete records and fit multivariable Cox model.
question: What bias should be considered?
betterApproach: Describe missingness, use principled imputation under stated assumptions, and perform sensitivity analysis.
maximalConclusion: Association in the selected complete-case subset may not represent the full cohort.

title: One minus Kaplan–Meier
study: Elderly cancer cohort; outcome is recurrence; death can occur first.
analysis: Censor deaths and plot 1−KM for recurrence.
question: What is wrong with the risk estimate?
expectedFindings: 1−KM treats competing deaths as potentially recurrent later
betterApproach: Estimate the cumulative incidence function; choose cause-specific or subdistribution regression by question.
maximalConclusion: The reported 42% is not a valid absolute recurrence probability with competing death.

title: Pathway from raw P values
study: 20,000 genes tested in 8 vs 8 tumors.
analysis: Select genes at raw P<.05 and run ORA using all human genes as background.
question: Identify two inference problems.
expectedFindings: Incorrect background if only measured genes eligible
betterApproach: Use effect sizes/FDR, an eligible tested-gene universe, and direction-aware ranked enrichment where appropriate.
maximalConclusion: The data generate a hypothesis about cell-cycle-related expression; activation is not established.

title: Batch equals disease
study: All tumors processed in April; all controls processed in June.
analysis: Apply Harmony and show a mixed UMAP.
claim: Disease-associated states remain after batch correction.
question: Can software identify the disease effect?
expectedFindings: Disease is perfectly confounded with batch
Correction may erase or invent signal
betterApproach: Acquire balanced batches or independent replication; narrow claims and perform sensitivity checks.
maximalConclusion: Disease and batch effects are inseparable in this dataset.

title: Cells split across CV folds
study: Single-cell classifier uses 20 patients and 80,000 cells.
analysis: Randomly split cells 80/20 for training and testing.
question: What leaked into the test set?
betterApproach: Group splits by patient; nest all feature selection and tuning in training folds.
maximalConclusion: Accuracy on new cells from already-seen patients may be high; new-patient performance is unknown.

title: Optimized biomarker cutpoint
study: A continuous marker is measured in 110 patients.
analysis: Search 40 cutpoints; report the smallest log-rank P=.004.
claim: The discovered cutoff robustly stratifies risk.
question: How should the evidence be labeled?
betterApproach: Prespecify/lock the chosen cutoff and evaluate it in independent data or validate the full selection procedure.
maximalConclusion: The cohort suggests a candidate cutpoint requiring validation.

title: One-marker cell label
study: A tumor cluster expresses EPCAM and also PTPRC in many cells.
analysis: Label as malignant epithelial solely because EPCAM is among top markers.
claim: A novel malignant state is identified.
question: What annotation checks are missing?
betterApproach: Use marker panels, doublet/ambient checks, inferred CNV or reference mapping, and patient distribution.
maximalConclusion: An EPCAM-expressing cluster is observed; malignant identity is uncertain.

title: Communication is not signaling
study: Tumor cells express TGFB1; fibroblasts express TGFBR genes.
analysis: CellChat assigns a high interaction score.
question: Where is the evidence ladder gap?
betterApproach: Add spatial/protein validation, receptor-pathway readouts, perturbation, phenotype, and rescue.
maximalConclusion: The expression pattern nominates a candidate communication axis.

title: Pseudotime as lineage
study: Cross-sectional tumors contain states ordered by pseudotime.
analysis: Root chosen from marker expression; one trajectory algorithm used.
claim: State A differentiates into state B in patients.
question: What can pseudotime establish?
betterApproach: Show topology sensitivity and add lineage, temporal, velocity, or perturbation evidence.
maximalConclusion: States form an expression continuum compatible with the chosen ordering.

title: Spatial neighbors
study: Exhausted T cells are closer to macrophages in tumor margins.
analysis: Nearest-neighbor enrichment is significant across all spots pooled.
question: Name the two largest claim problems.
betterApproach: Use patient-level spatial inference with compartment controls, orthogonal imaging, and functional perturbation.
maximalConclusion: The two states are spatially associated in sampled tissue.

title: Subtypes chosen for survival
study: Proteomic profiles permit cluster counts k=2…8.
analysis: Choose k=4 because it gives the smallest survival P value.
question: What is double dipping here?
expectedFindings: Same survival data tests selected k
betterApproach: Choose structure without outcome or validate the full selection externally; assess stability and assignment.
maximalConclusion: A four-cluster exploratory solution shows survival separation requiring validation.

title: No event count
study: Cohort includes 1,200 patients and 38 deaths.
analysis: Fit Cox model with 24 parameters after stepwise selection.
claim: All adjusted predictors are reliable because n is large.
question: Which number determines information more directly?
betterApproach: Reduce/prespecify complexity, consider penalization, and use resampling with uncertainty.
maximalConclusion: The fitted associations are likely unstable despite large total enrollment.

title: Non-significant means equal
study: Organoid drug responses: 4 independent lines per group.
analysis: Mean difference 22%, 95% CI −5% to 49%, P=.09.
question: What does the interval allow?
betterApproach: Report the estimate/CI and, if equivalence is the target, prespecify a clinically meaningful equivalence margin and design.
maximalConclusion: The data are inconclusive about a potentially meaningful difference.

title: Technical wells as n
study: One patient-derived organoid line is plated in 18 wells per condition.
analysis: Two-sample t test across wells gives P<.0001.
claim: Drug response generalizes to patient tumors.
question: What replication is present?
betterApproach: Repeat across independent organoid lines/donors and analyze hierarchical or summarized donor-level effects.
maximalConclusion: The drug changes the assay readout in this organoid line under these conditions.

title: C-index without calibration
study: External model validation reports C=.78.
analysis: No predicted risks or calibration are shown.
claim: The model is ready for clinical risk counseling.
question: Which property is untested?
betterApproach: Report calibration intercept/slope/plot, decision-relevant performance, and net benefit where appropriate.
maximalConclusion: The model shows ranking ability in this cohort; absolute-risk use is unproven.

title: Recalibration called validation
study: External cohort is used to adjust intercept, slope, and two coefficients.
analysis: Performance after updates is reported as external validation.
question: What result must be shown first?
betterApproach: Report original performance, then updating method and validation of the updated model.
maximalConclusion: Only local updated-model fit is described; original transportability is unknown.

title: Case-control diagnostic AUC
study: 50 obvious late-stage cases and 50 healthy volunteers.
analysis: Train/test a blood signature and report AUC=.99.
claim: The test is suitable for population screening.
question: What spectrum problem limits the claim?
expectedFindings: Cases/controls do not represent screening population
betterApproach: Evaluate a locked test prospectively among consecutive intended-use patients including relevant alternatives.
maximalConclusion: The signature distinguishes these extreme sampled groups.

title: Multi-omics concordance
study: Matched RNA and protein profiles from the same 30 tumors.
analysis: Both layers cluster into similar groups.
claim: Independent multi-omics validation confirms two biological subtypes.
question: Why is 'independent' incorrect?
expectedFindings: Concordance is cross-layer support, not sample validation
betterApproach: Use modality-specific analyses and validate a locked subtype classifier in independent patients/platforms.
maximalConclusion: Matched layers show concordant structure in the discovery cohort.

title: DE then cross-validation
study: All 200 patients are used to select 100 outcome-associated genes.
analysis: Five-fold CV trains a model using those fixed 100 genes.
question: Where is feature leakage?
expectedFindings: Outcomes from held-out folds selected genes
Pipeline, not final learner, must be validated
betterApproach: Repeat gene selection inside each training fold; use nested CV for tuning.
maximalConclusion: The reported AUC is contaminated and does not estimate new-patient performance.

title: Patient proportions pooled
study: Four responders and four nonresponders contribute unequal cell numbers.
analysis: Pool cells by response and compare cell-type counts with chi-square.
claim: Responders have more dendritic cells, P<10⁻⁶.
question: What should be plotted before any model?
betterApproach: Use sample-level or hierarchical compositional/count methods with patient as replicate.
maximalConclusion: Captured pooled-cell composition differs; patient-level response association is not established.

title: Median split
study: A continuous immune score is split at the sample median.
analysis: Kaplan–Meier curves differ at P=.04.
claim: High immune score is a validated prognostic biomarker.
question: What information and evidence were lost?
betterApproach: Model the continuous score with functional-form checks; predefine/validate any clinical threshold.
maximalConclusion: An exploratory median-defined association is observed in this cohort.

title: Post-treatment biomarker
study: Day-30 response biomarker predicts overall survival.
analysis: Include it as a baseline covariate from diagnosis in a Cox model.
claim: The marker independently predicts survival from diagnosis.
question: Which temporal issue arises?
betterApproach: Use a day-30 landmark among survivors or time-dependent modeling, with the changed target population explicit.
maximalConclusion: Among patients measured at day 30, the marker may have conditional prognostic value.

title: DCA without a decision
study: An omics score predicts progression.
analysis: Decision curves shown from thresholds 0–100% without stating an action.
question: What must threshold probability encode?
expectedFindings: Relative harm of false positive vs false negative
betterApproach: Define the decision and threshold range, compare realistic strategies, and interpret net benefit conditionally.
maximalConclusion: Clinical utility cannot be judged without a defined decision context.

title: AI invents a PMID
study: An AI response cites PMID 12345678 for a claimed single-cell trial.
analysis: Save citation and explanation directly to verified methods notes.
question: What must happen before verification status changes?
expectedFindings: Generated content remains pending by default
betterApproach: Resolve the identifier through an official metadata service, inspect the source, and record verification time/provenance.
maximalConclusion: The citation is unverified and must remain pending.

title: Figure story outruns evidence
study: Figures show association, spatial proximity, and in vitro knockdown.
analysis: Final model claims a universal human therapeutic mechanism and clinical efficacy.
claim: The study proves the target will benefit patients.
question: Where should the claim boundary stop?
expectedFindings: Association and proximity are not causal
In vitro perturbation supports context-specific function
betterApproach: State the supported in vitro functional role, distinguish human association, and specify missing in vivo/clinical evidence.
maximalConclusion: The target is associated with human disease and contributes to an in vitro phenotype under tested conditions.
